Specialize the closed subset to be empty and the target to be projective, retain the arbitrary-field regular projective alteration and its nonempty finite locus, and omit the normal-crossings boundary conclusion. title: Waldschmidt 2005 (Variations), Cor. 2.13, corrected: if (Λᵢⱼ) ∈ ℒ̃²ˣ³, Λ₁₁, Λ₂₁ ∈ ℝ ∪ iℝ, and 1, Λ₁₁, Λ₂₁ and 1, Λ₂₁, Λ₂₂, Λ₂₃, Λ̄₂₂, Λ̄₂₃ are Q̄-free, then Λ₁₁Λ₂₂ − Λ₂₁Λ₁₂ or Λ₁₁Λ₂₃ − Λ₂₁Λ₁₃ ∉ ℒ̃
author: @carlok
source: M. Waldschmidt, Variations on the six exponentials theorem, in Algebra and Number Theory (Hyderabad), Hindustan Book Agency, 2005, 338–355, Cor. 2.13 (p. 346; proof p. 347), with a corrected hypothesis. The printed Cor. 2.13 is false as stated: Λ₁₁ = 1, Λ₁₂ = Λ₁₃ = 0, Λ₂₁ = log 2, Λ₂₂ = Log(2 + i), Λ₂₃ = Log(3 + 2i) (principal logarithms) satisfy its hypotheses, the six numbers 1, log 2, Log(2 ± i), Log(3 ± 2i) being linearly independent over Q̄ by Baker's theorem, while Λ₁₁Λ₂₂ − Λ₂₁Λ₁₂ = Log(2 + i) and Λ₁₁Λ₂₃ − Λ₂₁Λ₁₃ = Log(3 + 2i) lie in ℒ. This node assumes instead that 1, Λ₁₁, Λ₂₁ are linearly independent over Q̄ (in place of 'Λ₂₁ ≠ 0 and Λ₁₁/Λ₂₁ transcendental'), as in M. Waldschmidt, The role of complex conjugation in transcendental number theory, 2005, Cor. 6.3; the printed hypothesis Λ₁₂, Λ₁₃ ∈ ℝ ∪ iℝ is not assumed. The printed proof applies Cor. 2.12 to the matrix with the conjugate columns (Λ̄₁ⱼ, Λ̄₂ⱼ), j = 2, 3; it needs signs on these columns when Λ₁₁ and Λ₂₁ are of different type (one real, the other purely imaginary). The proof here applies Role Cor. 6.3 to the columns (ε₂Λ̄₁ⱼ, ε₁Λ̄₂ⱼ), where Λ̄₁₁ = ε₁Λ₁₁ and Λ̄₂₁ = ε₂Λ₂₁ with ε₁, ε₂ ∈ {1, −1}. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 14 November 2026 (C. Perassi).

title: Random-order switching chain for single-cycle colored matchings
author: @dmilosch
source: Carolan, Childs, Coudron, Gilani, Miloschewsky, Podder, Algorithmic Wave-Particle Duality: Pathfinding in Welded Trees is Hard, https://arxiv.org/html/2611.05912v1#S4.SS4, Section 4.4, proof of Lemma 4.13. Equation (76) bounds a conditional matching partner by 1/(r-1). The following random-order residual-matrix swap process has the exact product-uniform output law. At remaining size r, a fixed forward matching entry is affected with probability at most 2/(m*r), conditional on the entire reference sample. Proper three-coloring gives N/2<=m<=N for each weld-color class, yielding the displayed 4/(N*r) certificate. Stages may be recorded jointly across the disjoint color classes because a fixed edge belongs to one class. Nonweld classes are copied. No quotient by the uncolored simple graph is taken, avoiding changes to the original sampling multiplicities. This child remains an open finite stochastic-construction obligation; the formal endpoint union bound, inverse-image transfer, harmonic bound, label lifting, and oracle lifting are supplied by the parent proof.

title: Conditional partner counts for single-cycle weld completions
author: @dmilosch
source: Carolan, Childs, Coudron, Gilani, Miloschewsky, Podder, Algorithmic Wave-Particle Duality: Pathfinding in Welded Trees is Hard, https://arxiv.org/html/2611.05912v1#S4.SS4, Section 4.4, proof of Lemma 4.13, equation (76) and its path-deletion/insertion and endpoint-symmetry argument. The probability inequality is multiplied by the positive completion count and residual denominator; empty and singleton cases are included trivially. Arbitrary records outside the tested color are handled by conditioning on complete assignments of the other colors and averaging, with independent nonweld coordinates factored out.

title: Fischler 2001, Th. 1.1: if k ≥ 3 and P = (λ₁X₁ + ⋯ + λₘXₘ)ᵏ has all its coefficients in ℒ̃, then P = aφᵏ with a ∈ ℒ̃ and φ a linear form with algebraic coefficients
author: @carlok
source: S. Fischler, Orbits under algebraic groups and logarithms of algebraic numbers, Acta Arith. 100 (2001), 167–187, Th. 1.1 (pp. 168–169), complex case; it is Th. 6.2 (1) (p. 184), here for any m. Fischler's ℒ, the Q̄-vector space spanned by 1 and the logarithms of algebraic numbers, is ℒ̃ here. The printed hypothesis that P is homogeneous of degree k is implied by P = Λᵏ and is omitted. The printed proof (of Th. 6.2, pp. 184–185) stops at n ≤ 1 and leaves implicit why a lies in ℒ̃; here a = c₀ᵏ is a Q̄-multiple of the coefficient λⱼᵏ of Xⱼᵏ in P. Proved from DiazModulus.fischler_linear_pow_prod_mem, DiazModulus.fischler_power_span_finrank and DiazModulus.fischler_rational_hull. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 18 November 2026 (C. Perassi).

title: Waldschmidt 2000 (DALAG), Remark p. 424: if E₀ is spanned by k-algebraically independent elements, then k + E₀ has Property (A B; C 0) (any k; E₀ ∩ k = {0} is automatic)
author: @carlok
source: M. Waldschmidt, Diophantine Approximation on Linear Algebraic Groups, Grundlehren der mathematischen Wissenschaften 326, Springer, 2000, Remark in §12.1.3 (p. 424), for any field k and without the hypothesis E₀ ∩ k = {0}, which follows from the algebraic independence (a non-zero c ∈ E₀ ∩ k would be a non-zero polynomial relation of degree at most 1). The statement of the Remark is correct, but its printed reason has a gap: Property (A B; C 0) is a property of the triple (k, K, E), not of the k-vector space E, so the k-linear isomorphism of k + E₀ with kX + E₀ in K(X) does not carry it. The proof here does not pass through K(X): the inductive proof of Prop. 12.2 (pp. 420–422) is run on k + E₀ directly (DiazModulus.dalag_prop_12_2_ii), with the hyperplane E₁ of its induction chosen to contain 1; the printed step "x ∉ E₁, hence x is transcendental over k(E₁)" (Lemma 12.3) fails for k + E₀ whenever 1 lies in the span of the entries but not in E₁. Proved from DiazModulus.dalag_prop_12_2_ii and DiazModulus.dalag_prop_12_13_i_ii_span. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 18 November 2026 (C. Perassi).

title: Fischler 2001, N.B. after Prop. 5.5: if M ∈ ℒ̃ⁿˣⁿ and no hyperplane of Matₙ(ℂ) defined over Q̄ contains both M and the identity, then dim C(M) ≤ (n² + 1)/2
author: @carlok
source: S. Fischler, Orbits under algebraic groups and logarithms of algebraic numbers, Acta Arith. 100 (2001), 167–187, N.B. after Prop. 5.5 (p. 183): Th. 1.2 (p. 169), complex case, still holds when the hypothesis that the n² entries of M are Q̄-free is replaced by: no hyperplane of Matₙ(ℂ) defined over Q̄ contains both M and the identity. Hyperplanes are vector hyperplanes (convention of p. 169), and one defined over Q̄ is the kernel of a non-zero linear form with algebraic coefficients (p. 170). Fischler's ℒ, the Q̄-vector space spanned by 1 and the logarithms of algebraic numbers, is ℒ̃ here. The N.B. has no separate proof: the printed proof of Th. 1.2 (pp. 181–183) uses the freeness only to show that algebraic A, B with Tr(M(AB − BA)) = 0 commute, and the hypothesis gives that: when AB − BA ≠ 0, the kernel of N ↦ Tr(N(AB − BA)) is a hyperplane defined over Q̄ that contains M and the identity. Proved from DiazModulus.fischler_prop_5_5 and DiazModulus.remond_commuting_subspaces. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 18 November 2026 (C. Perassi).

title: Waldschmidt 2000 (DALAG), Prop. 12.2 (D. Roy): if E is spanned by k-algebraically independent elements, every matrix over E is k-equivalent to (A B; C 0) with A regular or empty
author: @carlok
source: M. Waldschmidt, Diophantine Approximation on Linear Algebraic Groups, Grundlehren der mathematischen Wissenschaften 326, Springer, 2000, Prop. 12.2 (p. 419), Proposition 1 of D. Roy (1990), for any field k, by the proof of pp. 420–422; the other proof (p. 424) assumes k infinite and is not used. The zero-size A of the statement is r = 0. In the Remark after Prop. 12.2 (p. 419) the sizes printed for the second and third examples are slips (rows linearly independent: d′ = 0 and ℓ′ = d; columns linearly independent: d′ = d − ℓ and ℓ′ = ℓ); every r ≤ min(s, t) is allowed here, so the three shapes are covered. Proved from DiazModulus.dalag_prop_12_2_ii and DiazModulus.dalag_prop_12_13_i_ii_span. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 18 November 2026 (C. Perassi).

title: Fischler 2001, Th. 6.2 (2): if P = (λ₁X₁ + ⋯ + λₘXₘ)² has all its coefficients in ℒ̃, then P = (aφ₁ + bφ₂)² with a, b ∈ ℂ and φ₁, φ₂ linear forms with algebraic coefficients
author: @carlok
source: S. Fischler, Orbits under algebraic groups and logarithms of algebraic numbers, Acta Arith. 100 (2001), 167–187, Th. 6.2, part 2 (p. 184), complex case, without the printed hypothesis m ≥ 2 (for m ≤ 2 the conclusion is immediate). Fischler's ℒ, the Q̄-vector space spanned by 1 and the logarithms of algebraic numbers, is ℒ̃ here. The printed hypothesis that P is homogeneous of degree 2 is implied by P = Λ² and is omitted. Proved from DiazModulus.fischler_linear_pow_prod_mem, DiazModulus.fischler_power_span_finrank and DiazModulus.fischler_rational_hull. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 18 November 2026 (C. Perassi).

source: S. Fischler, Orbits under algebraic groups and logarithms of algebraic numbers, Acta Arith. 100 (2001), 167–187, Lemma 6.1 (p. 184).
